diff --git a/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/subagent_accumulation_test.go b/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/subagent_accumulation_test.go

@@ -0,0 +1,171 @@
+//go:build integration
+
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
+)
+
+// TestSubagentAccumulation_Issue591 reproduces the issue #591 shape: multiple
+// subagent sessions end with uncommitted files that never overlap with a later
+// parent-session commit. The stale ENDED subagent sessions must be force-condensed
+// on that later commit so they do not accumulate and get re-processed forever.
+func TestSubagentAccumulation_Issue591(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
+
+	type subagentInfo struct {
+		SessionID string
+		File      string
+	}
+
+	t.Log("Phase 1: start parent session and create stale ended subagent sessions")
+
+	parent := env.NewSession()
+	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(parent.ID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit for parent failed: %v", err)
+	}
+	parent.TranscriptBuilder.AddUserMessage("Use subagents to investigate the work and then create the parent file.")
+
+	const numSubagents = 4
+	subagents := make([]subagentInfo, 0, numSubagents)
+
+	for i := 0; i < numSubagents; i++ {
+		sub := env.NewSession()
+		file := fmt.Sprintf("subagent_work_%d.go", i)
+		content := fmt.Sprintf("package main\n\nfunc SubagentWork%d() {}\n", i)
+
+		if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(sub.ID); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit for subagent %d failed: %v", i, err)
+		}
+
+		env.WriteFile(file, content)
+		sub.CreateTranscript("Create "+file, []FileChange{
+			{Path: file, Content: content},
+		})
+
+		if err := env.SimulateStop(sub.ID, sub.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("SimulateStop for subagent %d failed: %v", i, err)
+		}
+		if err := env.SimulateSessionEnd(sub.ID); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("SimulateSessionEnd for subagent %d failed: %v", i, err)
+		}
+
+		state, err := env.GetSessionState(sub.ID)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("GetSessionState for subagent %d failed: %v", i, err)
+		}
+		if state == nil {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d session state missing", i)
+		}
+		if state.Phase != session.PhaseEnded {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d phase = %s, want ended", i, state.Phase)
+		}
+		if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d FilesTouched should be non-empty before cleanup", i)
+		}
+		if state.StepCount == 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d StepCount should be > 0 before cleanup", i)
+		}
+		if state.FullyCondensed {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d should not be FullyCondensed before cleanup", i)
+		}
+
+		staleEndedAt := time.Now().Add(-2 * time.Hour)
+		state.EndedAt = &staleEndedAt
+		if err := env.WriteSessionState(sub.ID, state); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("WriteSessionState for subagent %d failed: %v", i, err)
+		}
+
+		taskToolUseID := fmt.Sprintf("toolu_parent_subagent_%d", i)
+		parent.TranscriptBuilder.AddTaskToolUse(taskToolUseID, "Create "+file)
+		parent.TranscriptBuilder.AddTaskToolResult(taskToolUseID, sub.ID)
+
+		subagents = append(subagents, subagentInfo{
+			SessionID: sub.ID,
+			File:      file,
+		})
+	}
+
+	t.Log("Phase 2: parent commits unrelated work")
+
+	parentFile := "parent_work.go"
+	parentContent := "package main\n\nfunc ParentWork() {}\n"
+	env.WriteFile(parentFile, parentContent)
+	parentToolUseID := parent.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolUse("mcp__acp__Write", parentFile, parentContent)
+	parent.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolResult(parentToolUseID)
+	parent.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("Done.")
+	if err := parent.TranscriptBuilder.WriteToFile(parent.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("failed to write parent transcript: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	if err := env.SimulateStop(parent.ID, parent.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop for parent failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Parent commit", parentFile)
+
+	t.Log("Phase 3: verify stale ended subagent sessions were force-condensed")
+
+	for i, sub := range subagents {
+		state, err := env.GetSessionState(sub.SessionID)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("GetSessionState after parent commit for subagent %d failed: %v", i, err)
+		}
+		if state == nil {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d session state missing after parent commit", i)
+		}
+		if state.Phase != session.PhaseEnded {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d phase after parent commit = %s, want ended", i, state.Phase)
+		}
+		if state.StepCount != 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d StepCount = %d, want 0 after force-condense", i, state.StepCount)
+		}
+		if len(state.FilesTouched) != 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d FilesTouched = %v, want empty after force-condense", i, state.FilesTouched)
+		}
+		if !state.FullyCondensed {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d should be FullyCondensed after force-condense", i)
+		}
+	}
+
+	t.Log("Phase 4: make another unrelated commit and verify fully-condensed subagents stay skipped")
+
+	followUp := env.NewSession()
+	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(followUp.ID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit for follow-up session failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	followUpFile := "follow_up.go"
+	followUpContent := "package main\n\nfunc FollowUp() {}\n"
+	env.WriteFile(followUpFile, followUpContent)
+	followUp.CreateTranscript("Create "+followUpFile, []FileChange{
+		{Path: followUpFile, Content: followUpContent},
+	})
+	if err := env.SimulateStop(followUp.ID, followUp.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop for follow-up session failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Follow-up commit", followUpFile)
+
+	for i, sub := range subagents {
+		state, err := env.GetSessionState(sub.SessionID)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("GetSessionState after follow-up commit for subagent %d failed: %v", i, err)
+		}
+		if state == nil {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d session state missing after follow-up commit", i)
+		}
+		if !state.FullyCondensed {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d should remain FullyCondensed after follow-up commit", i)
+		}
+		if state.StepCount != 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("subagent %d StepCount = %d after follow-up commit, want 0", i, state.StepCount)
+		}
+	}
+}
diff --git a/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go b/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go
index ea571c78..caee0966 100644
--- a/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go
+++ b/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go
@@ -619,7 +619,22 @@ func handleLifecycleSessionEnd(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent
 	if err := markSessionEnded(ctx, event, event.SessionID); err != nil {
 		logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to mark session ended",
 			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
+		// Don't attempt eager condense if we couldn't even mark the session ended —
+		// the session state may be in an inconsistent state.
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	// Eagerly condense session data so PostCommit doesn't have to process it.
+	// This prevents zombie ENDED sessions from accumulating and causing O(N)
+	// overhead on every future commit (GitHub issue #591).
+	// Fail-open: if this fails, PostCommit's force-condense safety net catches it.
+	strat := GetStrategy(ctx)
+	if err := strat.CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed(ctx, event.SessionID); err != nil {
+		logging.Warn(logCtx, "eager condense on session stop failed",
+			slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
+			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
 	}
+
 	return nil
 }

+package strategy
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
+
+	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
+	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/object"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// TestPostCommit_Issue591_SubagentScaleRegression is a regression test for GitHub
+// issue #591: accumulated stale ENDED sessions caused O(N) overhead on every commit
+// (~73-103ms per session, indefinitely). After the fix, they are force-condensed on
+// the first PostCommit and skipped via FullyCondensed on all subsequent commits.
+//
+// Behavioral coverage (FullyCondensed/StepCount/FilesTouched assertions) lives in
+// TestPostCommit_EndedSessionCarryForward_ForceCondensedWithoutOverlap. This test
+// focuses on the performance contract: the second PostCommit must be significantly
+// faster than the first once sessions are marked FullyCondensed.
+func TestPostCommit_Issue591_SubagentScaleRegression(t *testing.T) {
+	const sessionCount = 10
+
+	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
+
+	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
+
+	// Create sessions with shadow branches, then mark them stale ENDED.
+	// Each session's FilesTouched = ["test.txt"], which won't overlap with the
+	// unrelated.txt commit below, triggering the force-condense path.
+	for i := range sessionCount {
+		sessionID := fmt.Sprintf("ended-session-%d", i)
+		setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)
+		state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		staleAt := time.Now().Add(-(forceCondenseThreshold + time.Minute))
+		state.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
+		state.EndedAt = &staleAt
+		require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))
+	}
+
+	// Commit an unrelated file — no overlap with any session's FilesTouched.
+	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "unrelated.txt"), []byte("user work"), 0o644))
+	_, err = wt.Add("unrelated.txt")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = wt.Commit("unrelated\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n", &git.CommitOptions{
+		Author: &object.Signature{Name: "User", Email: "user@test.com", When: time.Now()},
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
+
+	// First PostCommit: force-condenses all stale ENDED sessions.
+	firstStart := time.Now()
+	require.NoError(t, s.PostCommit(context.Background()))
+	firstElapsed := time.Since(firstStart)
+
+	// Create second commit — all sessions are now FullyCondensed and should be skipped.
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "second.txt"), []byte("second"), 0o644))
+	_, err = wt.Add("second.txt")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = wt.Commit("second\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: b1b2b3b4b5b6\n", &git.CommitOptions{
+		Author: &object.Signature{Name: "User", Email: "user@test.com", When: time.Now()},

+		}

+		}
+		if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 {

+		}
+		if state.StepCount == 0 {

+package strategy

+import (
+	"context"

+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// TestPostCommit_Issue591_SubagentScaleRegression is a regression test for GitHub
+// issue #591: accumulated stale ENDED sessions caused O(N) overhead on every commit
+// (~73-103ms per session, indefinitely). After the fix, they are force-condensed on
+// the first PostCommit and skipped via FullyCondensed on all subsequent commits.
+//
+// Behavioral coverage (FullyCondensed/StepCount/FilesTouched assertions) lives in
+// TestPostCommit_EndedSessionCarryForward_ForceCondensedWithoutOverlap. This test
+// focuses on the performance contract: the second PostCommit must be significantly
+// faster than the first once sessions are marked FullyCondensed.
+func TestPostCommit_Issue591_SubagentScaleRegression(t *testing.T) {
+	const sessionCount = 10
+
+	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
+
+	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
+
+	// Create sessions with shadow branches, then mark them stale ENDED.
+	// Each session's FilesTouched = ["test.txt"], which won't overlap with the
+	// unrelated.txt commit below, triggering the force-condense path.
+	for i := range sessionCount {
+		sessionID := fmt.Sprintf("ended-session-%d", i)
+		setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)
+		state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		staleAt := time.Now().Add(-(forceCondenseThreshold + time.Minute))
+		state.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
+		state.EndedAt = &staleAt
+		require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))
+	}
+
+	// Commit an unrelated file — no overlap with any session's FilesTouched.
+	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "unrelated.txt"), []byte("user work"), 0o644))
+	_, err = wt.Add("unrelated.txt")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = wt.Commit("unrelated\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n", &git.CommitOptions{
+		Author: &object.Signature{Name: "User", Email: "user@test.com", When: time.Now()},
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
+
+	// First PostCommit: force-condenses all stale ENDED sessions.
+	firstStart := time.Now()
+	require.NoError(t, s.PostCommit(context.Background()))
+	firstElapsed := time.Since(firstStart)
+
+	// Create second commit — all sessions are now FullyCondensed and should be skipped.
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "second.txt"), []byte("second"), 0o644))
+	_, err = wt.Add("second.txt")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = wt.Commit("second\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: b1b2b3b4b5b6\n", &git.CommitOptions{
+		Author: &object.Signature{Name: "User", Email: "user@test.com", When: time.Now()},
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
+
+	s2 := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
+	secondStart := time.Now()
+	require.NoError(t, s2.PostCommit(context.Background()))
+	secondElapsed := time.Since(secondStart)
+
+	// Second PostCommit must be significantly faster — sessions are FullyCondensed and skipped.
+	assert.Less(t, secondElapsed, firstElapsed/2,
+		"second PostCommit should be much faster once sessions are FullyCondensed (issue #591 regression)")
+	t.Logf("first PostCommit (%d stale sessions): %v, second (all skipped): %v",
+		sessionCount, firstElapsed, secondElapsed)
+}

+		state.StepCount = 0
+		state.FullyCondensed = true // FilesTouched is already empty (checked above)
+		return s.saveSessionState(ctx, state)

+			slog.String("error", err.Error()),

+	}

+	state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
+	state.AttributionBaseCommit = state.BaseCommit
+	state.PromptAttributions = nil
+	state.PendingPromptAttribution = nil

+		)
+	}

{"body":"Fixes O(N) commit-time overhead caused by stale ENDED sessions accumulating and being re-processed on every
   PostCommit (~73-103ms per session, indefinitely). Tracked as issue #591.                                  
                                                                                                             
  Two complementary fixes:                                                                                   
                                                                                                           
  - Eager condense on session stop (CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed): When a session ends via the stop hook and
   has no FilesTouched, its checkpoint data is immediately condensed to entire/checkpoints/v1 and the session
   is marked FullyCondensed. PostCommit skips these sessions entirely on all future commits.                 
  - Force-condense safety net in PostCommit: ENDED sessions that are older than 1 hour and still have      
  FilesTouched with no commit overlap are now force-condensed instead of being carried forward forever. This 
  catches sessions the eager path couldn't handle (older CLI versions, crashes, or sessions that had
  FilesTouched at stop time — the primary subagent accumulation shape from #591).                            
                                                                                                           
  Key design choices:                                                                                        
  - CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed intentionally keeps Phase = ENDED (unlike CondenseSessionByID which resets
  to IDLE) and skips sessions with FilesTouched so PostCommit's carry-forward tracking still works for those 
  - The 1-hour forceCondenseThreshold gives users a window to commit a session's files in a separate commit 
  before the safety net fires                                                                                
  - Force-condensed sessions skip carry-forward computation entirely — FilesTouched is cleared to nil

content.text:
Good — `GetStrategy` returns the concrete type directly, so calling `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` on it works without interface changes. I've now read the full diff and key context. Here's my review:

---

## PR Review: `perf/force-condense-ended-sessions` (#599)

### Overall

Well-structured fix for a real performance problem. The two-layer approach (eager condense on stop + PostCommit safety net) is sound. Test coverage is thorough. A few issues worth addressing:

### Issues

**1. `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` silently swallows its own error contract (medium)**

`lifecycle.go:632` calls `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` and logs a warning on error — but the method itself already returns `nil` (fail-open) for most internal failures. The only error it *does* return is `"failed to load session state"` and `"failed to save session state"`. The logging in `lifecycle.go` is fine, but the comment says "Fail-open: if this fails, PostCommit's force-condense safety net catches it" — yet the PostCommit safety net only catches sessions with `FilesTouched` (the `isStaleEnded` path in `HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched`). Sessions with `FilesTouched == nil` and `StepCount > 0` that fail eager condense have no safety net. Consider whether this gap matters in practice (probably rare — `saveSessionState` failure suggests disk issues).

**2. `checkpointID` logging inconsistency in `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` (nit)**

Line 941: `result.CheckpointID.String()` — but `checkpointID` is also available in scope and was what you passed to `CondenseSession`. These should be the same, but using `result.CheckpointID` is cleaner since it's the one that was actually used. This is fine as-is.

**3. Benchmark test `TestPostCommit_Issue591_SubagentScaleRegression` is timing-sensitive (low)**

`assert.Less(t, secondElapsed, firstElapsed/2)` — on a heavily loaded CI machine, the first PostCommit could be fast enough that `firstElapsed/2` is under the noise floor. With 10 sessions this is probably fine, but consider if this could flake. The `t.Logf` at the end helps debug if it does.

**4. Force-condense passes `nil` for `committedFileSet` — verify `CondenseSession` handles this correctly (medium)**

At `manual_commit_hooks.go:691`, the force-condense path passes `nil` for `committedFileSet` (where normal condense passes the actual set). This means `CondenseSession` will include *all* `FilesTouched` in the checkpoint metadata. The comment at line 920 in `manual_commit_condensation.go` says "Condense with nil committedFiles (include all FilesTouched)" — good, this is intentional. But then at line 664, `state.FilesTouched = nil` clears them. The session data on `entire/checkpoints/v1` preserves the full file list, but the session state no longer tracks what was touched. This is the correct behavior for a force-condensed session (it's done), but worth confirming that nothing downstream reads `FilesTouched` from the state file post-condensation and expects it populated.

**5. `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` doesn't check `state.Phase` (low)**

The method is called from `handleLifecycleSessionEnd`, which just called `markSessionEnded`. But `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` doesn't verify `state.Phase == ENDED`. If somehow the state was concurrently modified between `markSessionEnded` and this call (another session process?), it could mark an ACTIVE session as `FullyCondensed`. Low risk given the call site, but a defensive check would be cheap.

**6. `FullyCondensed` marking condition broadened — verify no regression (medium)**

The condition changed from:
```go
if handler.condensed && state.Phase == session.PhaseEnded && len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 {
```
to:
```go
if state.Phase == session.PhaseEnded && len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 && (handler.condensed || !hasNew) {
```

The `!hasNew` case handles empty ENDED sessions that never had content. This is correct (the `TestPostCommit_EmptyEndedSession_MarkedFullyCondensed` test covers it). But double-check: could `!hasNew` be true for an ENDED session that *did* have content but was already condensed by the eager path? If so, `FullyCondensed` would already be `true` from eager condense, so this is a no-op — safe.

### Test Quality

The test coverage is excellent:
- Unit tests for both guard conditions and happy path of `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed`
- PostCommit tests for force-condense, recent-not-force-condensed, and empty-ended
- Integration test for the full subagent accumulation scenario (#591)
- Regression benchmark verifying the O(N) → O(1) improvement
- Existing carry-forward test updated to match new behavior

### Minor Nits

- The PR title says "force condense ended orphaned ended sessions" — double "ended" looks like a typo
- `accumulation_bench_test.go:384` uses `const sessionCount = 10` — consider a comment noting this is deliberately small to avoid CI timeouts while still being large enough to measure the difference

### Summary

The approach is solid: eager condense as the primary path, PostCommit force-condense as safety net, with a 1-hour grace period. The fail-open design is appropriate. Issues #1 and #4 are worth thinking about but likely acceptable. Ship it.

Now I have the full picture. Here's the answer:

---

The short answer: **PostCommit can't just load the "current" session because there isn't one.** The post-commit hook runs in a bare git hook context with no session ID. It has to discover which sessions exist.

Here's the actual cost breakdown of `PostCommit`:

### What's actually happening

1. **`store.List()`** (`session/state.go:401`) — reads `.git/entire-sessions/*.json` files. These are tiny JSON metadata files (a few KB each — `SessionID`, `BaseCommit`, `WorktreeID`, `Phase`, `FilesTouched`, etc.). Reading 20 of them is sub-millisecond. This is NOT where the 148s comes from.

2. **`listAllSessionStates()`** (`manual_commit_session.go:60`) — for each session state, it resolves the shadow branch ref via `repo.Reference()`. This is a git ref lookup per session — also cheap.

3. **`postCommitProcessSession()`** — this is where the real cost is. Per session:
   - Resolves shadow branch ref + commit + tree (git object reads)
   - `sessionHasNewContent()` — reads transcript from shadow branch tree to compare line counts
   - `filesOverlapWithContent()` — content-aware diff between shadow tree and HEAD tree
   - `CondenseSession()` — builds new tree on `entire/checkpoints/v1`, writes blobs
   - `filesWithRemainingAgentChanges()` — another tree comparison for carry-forward

The 190 MB figure you're seeing isn't from reading session state files — those are kilobytes. It's from git object I/O: resolving shadow branch trees, reading transcript blobs from those trees, and tree comparisons. Each session's shadow branch may reference large transcript files (the "~17 MB" you mentioned per session is likely the transcript blob in the shadow branch tree, not the state file).

### Why you can't just load "the active session"

PostCommit legitimately needs all sessions for this worktree because:

1. **Multiple concurrent sessions** — a parent + N subagent sessions can all be active simultaneously, all needing condensation on the same commit
2. **ENDED sessions with carry-forward** — an old session's `FilesTouched` might overlap with this commit's files, requiring condensation
3. **Base commit updates** — even non-condensed active sessions need `BaseCommit` advanced to the new HEAD

### What this PR actually fixes

The PR's `FullyCondensed` flag is exactly the right optimization for the *inner loop* — it short-circuits at line 900-901 before any git object I/O:

```go
if state.FullyCondensed && state.Phase == session.PhaseEnded {
    continue  // No shadow branch resolution, no tree reads, nothing
}
```

The eager condense on session stop (`CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed`) means most subagent sessions are already `FullyCondensed` before PostCommit even runs — so they're skipped at the JSON metadata level, never touching git objects.

### The remaining opportunity

If you're still seeing 148s with 20 sessions *after* this PR, the remaining cost is from sessions that *aren't* `FullyCondensed` yet (e.g., ACTIVE sessions, recently-ended sessions within the 1-hour threshold, or sessions with `FilesTouched`). The real bottleneck there is `sessionHasNewContent()` reading transcript blobs from shadow branch trees — that's where the per-session ~7-8s comes from. To optimize that further, you'd want to cache transcript line counts in the session state file (avoid reading the blob at all) rather than reducing the session scan.

content.text: OK, now let me look at how the `postCommitUpdateBaseCommitOnly` path (no trailer) also scans everything.

You're right that there's an optimization opportunity. Here's what's going on and what could be done:

### The current flow

```
PostCommit
  → findSessionsForWorktree
    → listAllSessionStates          ← reads ALL .json files from .git/entire-sessions/
      → for each: repo.Reference()  ← ref lookup per session (packed-refs scan)
    → filter by WorktreePath
  → for each session:
    → FullyCondensed skip (line 900)           ← cheap, but we already did the I/O
    → resolve shadow branch ref + tree         ← git object reads
    → sessionHasNewContent                     ← reads transcript BLOB from shadow tree
    → condensation / carry-forward             ← more git object I/O
```

The expensive part per session is **not** reading the state JSON (tiny) — it's the `repo.Reference()` call in `listAllSessionStates` (line 89-91) which does a packed-refs scan for each session, and then the shadow tree resolution + transcript blob read in `postCommitProcessSession`.

### Your insight is correct

The shadow branch name is deterministic: `entire/<baseCommit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`. In PostCommit, we know:
- The **parent commit** hash (the base commit for sessions active before this commit)
- The **worktree hash** (from `paths.WorktreeRoot`)

So we could compute the one shadow branch that matters, check if it exists with a single ref lookup, and read session IDs from its commit trailers — instead of scanning all 20 state files and doing 20 ref lookups.

### But there's a complication

Sessions don't all share the same `BaseCommit`. Consider:

1. **Active sessions** — BaseCommit = parent of HEAD (the expected shadow branch). These are the common case.
2. **ENDED sessions with carry-forward** — BaseCommit could be from several commits ago (their shadow branch got carried forward, or `BaseCommit` wasn't advanced because they're ENDED per PR #359). Their shadow branch is `entire/<olderHash[:7]>-<worktreeHash>`.
3. **Sessions needing migration** — BaseCommit changed due to stash/pull/rebase.

So the "one shadow branch" approach only covers case 1. Cases 2 and 3 require either scanning state files or enumerating all `entire/*` refs.

### What would actually work

A hybrid approach for PostCommit:

```
1. Compute expected shadow branch: entire/<parent[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>
2. Single ref lookup — if it exists, read commit trailers → session IDs
3. Load ONLY those session state files (the "hot" sessions)
4. For FullyCondensed bookkeeping + stale ENDED carry-forward:
   do a lazy scan of remaining state files, but SKIP the ref lookup
   for any that are FullyCondensed (just read the JSON, check the flag, move on)
```

The key win: `listAllSessionStates` currently does `repo.Reference()` for **every** session including FullyCondensed ones. That's the O(sessions × packed-refs-size) cost the perf tests call out. You could:

1. **Short-circuit `FullyCondensed` sessions in `listAllSessionStates`** — skip the ref lookup entirely. The JSON parse is negligible; it's the ref resolution that's expensive.
2. **For the trailer path**, use the shadow branch as an index to find the 1-3 sessions that actually matter, avoiding the full state file scan.

That said — this PR's eager condense already means most subagent sessions become `FullyCondensed` *before* PostCommit runs. So the 20-session scan drops to ~1-3 non-FullyCondensed sessions that actually need processing. The remaining cost is just the JSON reads + ref lookups for the FullyCondensed ones, which could be eliminated by the short-circuit in `listAllSessionStates`.

Want me to look at what that `listAllSessionStates` short-circuit would look like? It's a small change — skip `repo.Reference()` when `state.FullyCondensed && state.Phase == PhaseEnded` — and it'd eliminate the packed-refs scan overhead for the 17+ sessions that are already done.

content.text:
Right. So the shadow branch tree contains `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/full.jsonl` — one directory per session. Multiple sessions can share the same shadow branch (same base commit + worktree). The tree itself is an index of which sessions have data.

Here's the picture:

**Shadow branch tree structure:**
```
.entire/metadata/
  session-A/
    full.jsonl          ← transcript
    prompt.txt
  session-B/
    full.jsonl
    prompt.txt
  session-C/
    ...
file1.txt               ← agent-modified files
file2.txt
```

So yes — you could enumerate session IDs directly from the shadow tree by listing entries under `.entire/metadata/`, without ever touching `.git/entire-sessions/` state files. The tree already knows which sessions wrote to this branch.

The optimized PostCommit flow would be:

```
1. Compute shadow branch: entire/<parent[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>
2. Single ref lookup → resolve tree (you need this anyway for condensation)
3. List .entire/metadata/* entries in tree → session IDs with data
4. Load ONLY those session state files from .git/entire-sessions/
5. Process them
```

This replaces the current:
```
1. ReadDir(.git/entire-sessions/) → all 20 .json files
2. Parse each one
3. repo.Reference() for each → 20 packed-refs scans
4. Filter by worktree path
5. Filter FullyCondensed
6. Process remaining
```

The win is significant: instead of 20 state file reads + 20 ref lookups, you do 1 ref lookup + 1 tree traversal (which you're already doing) + N state file reads where N is typically 1-3.

**The catch** is sessions that are on a *different* shadow branch than the expected one — ENDED sessions whose `BaseCommit` is from an older commit. But those are exactly the sessions this PR is trying to clean up. After this PR's eager condense, they'd be `FullyCondensed` and shouldn't need processing at all. The force-condense safety net in PostCommit is for sessions the eager path missed.

So the question becomes: is the safety net important enough to keep the full scan, or could you accept that sessions missed by eager condense just get cleaned up by `entire doctor` / the next session stop? If you can accept that, the shadow-tree-as-index approach eliminates the O(all sessions) scan entirely. If you can't, you'd still need a fallback scan but could make it much cheaper (read just the `Phase` and `FullyCondensed` fields without ref lookups).

OK. So after condensation: `BaseCommit` is set to `newHead` (line 1160) and the shadow branch is queued for deletion (line 1156). After carry-forward, the data moves to a new shadow branch at the new BaseCommit.

Here's the complete invariant chain:

**For ENDED sessions that are NOT condensed:**
- `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` **skips** them (line 1196) → `BaseCommit` stays frozen
- Their data stays on the original shadow branch (`entire/<frozenBaseCommit[:7]>-<wt>`)
- This means: `BaseCommit` always points to the shadow branch where the data lives

**For condensed sessions (including carry-forward):**
- `BaseCommit` advances to `newHead` (line 1160)
- Old shadow branch queued for deletion
- Carry-forward creates new data on the new shadow branch (at the new `BaseCommit`)

So:

No, you don't need the time-based force condensation. The shadow branch gives you a structural signal that's strictly better. Here's why:

When PostCommit runs after a commit with parent P:

1. The "current" shadow branch is `entire/<P[:7]>-<worktreeHash>`
2. Any ENDED session whose `BaseCommit` == P has its data on this branch — it's still "relevant" (might overlap with committed files on the next commit)
3. Any ENDED session whose `BaseCommit` != P is on a **different** shadow branch — it was never condensed into any commit since it ended, and since `BaseCommit` is frozen for ENDED sessions, it can **never** be on the current branch again

Case 3 is the structural proof of staleness. These sessions are unreachable through normal condensation — no future commit will have its parent match their `BaseCommit`. They're permanently orphaned from the commit DAG's perspective.

So the rule becomes:

```
if state.Phase == ENDED && state.BaseCommit != parentOfHEAD {
    // Structurally stale — condense immediately, no time threshold
}
```

This is cleaner than the time-based approach because:
- **Deterministic** — no arbitrary 1-hour window
- **Immediate** — cleans up on the very first commit after the session becomes unreachable, not after waiting
- **No false positives** — if `BaseCommit` == parent, the session genuinely could still overlap with a future commit touching its files
- **No false negatives** — if `BaseCommit` != parent and the session is ENDED, there's no path back to relevance

Combined with the shadow-tree-as-index optimization, PostCommit becomes:

```
1. Resolve shadow branch for entire/<parent[:7]>-<worktreeHash>
2. List .entire/metadata/* in shadow tree → "hot" session IDs
3. Load only those state files → process normally (overlap check, condense, carry-forward)
4. Cheap scan of remaining .git/entire-sessions/*.json:
   - FullyCondensed? skip
   - ENDED + BaseCommit != parent? → condense immediately (structurally stale)
   - ACTIVE? → shouldn't happen (active sessions are on the current branch), but handle gracefully
```

Step 4 only needs to parse the JSON and check two fields — no `repo.Reference()`, no tree reads, no transcript I/O.

content.text:
Exactly. That's the beauty of filtering by `BaseCommit == parent of HEAD` — it naturally handles branch switching without any special logic.

Trace through the scenario:

```
Branch A: ... → H1 → H2 → H3
                 ↑
                 Session S1 (ENDED, BaseCommit=H1)

User switches to Branch B: ... → H4 → H5
```

User commits on branch B, parent = H4. PostCommit runs:
- S1's `BaseCommit` = H1, which is ≠ H4 → **skip**
- S1 is untouched, correctly left for when the user returns to branch A

User switches back to branch A, commits, parent = H3:
- S1's `BaseCommit` = H1, still ≠ H3 → **skip** again

S1 is on a different shadow branch either way. It's not on the current shadow branch, so it's never loaded, never processed.

This means the `BaseCommit == parent` filter is the only filter you need. It collapses three concerns into one check:

| Scenario | BaseCommit == parent? | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Active session on current branch | Yes | Process normally |
| ENDED session, just ended | Yes | Process (overlap check, condense) |
| ENDED session from older commit (issue #591) | No | Skip |
| Session from a different branch | No | Skip |

And for the #591 sessions that get skipped — they were already handled by eager condense on session stop. The PostCommit force-condense safety net becomes unnecessary because:

1. **Primary path**: eager condense at session stop handles it
2. **Missed by eager** (crash, older CLI): they sit as inert JSON files, skipped by PostCommit at O(0) cost, cleaned up by `entire doctor`
3. **No O(N) overhead** — PostCommit never touches them

So the time-based `forceCondenseThreshold` can go. The architecture simplifies to:

```
PostCommit:
  1. parent = HEAD~1
  2. shadow branch = entire/<parent[:7]>-<wt>
  3. List .entire/metadata/* in shadow tree → session IDs
  4. Load only those state files
  5. Process (condense, carry-forward, etc.)
  6. Done — everything else is invisible

Session stop:
  Eager condense (existing CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed)

entire doctor:
  Catches stragglers
```

PostCommit goes from scanning 20 sessions to loading 1-3. The `findSessionsForWorktree` + `listAllSessionStates` + 20 ref lookups are all eliminated. Want me to sketch out what that implementation would look like?

## Context

The current PR (#599) fixes O(N) PostCommit overhead from stale ENDED sessions with two mechanisms:
1. Eager condense on session stop (CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed) - KEEP THIS
2. Force-condense safety net in PostCommit with 1-hour time threshold - REPLACE THIS

We're replacing mechanism 2 with a structural approach: use the shadow branch tree as an index of which sessions need processing, and skip everything else based on BaseCommit != parent of HEAD.

## Key Insight

- Shadow branch name is `entire/<baseCommit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`
- The shadow tree contains `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/` directories — one per session with data
- ENDED sessions' BaseCommit is frozen (updateBaseCommitIfChanged skips non-active sessions)
- So: BaseCommit == parent of HEAD means the session is on the current shadow branch. BaseCommit != parent means it's either from a different branch or structurally stale — skip it either way.

- `forceCondenseThreshold` constant and `isStaleEnded()` function in `manual_commit_hooks.go`
- The `case h.hasNew && isStaleEnded(state)` branch in `HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched`

2. Loop over all, skip FullyCondensed

1. Compute shadow branch: `entire/<parent[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`
2. Single ref lookup → resolve shadow tree
3. List `.entire/metadata/*` entries in shadow tree → session IDs with data on this branch
4. Load ONLY those session state files
5. Process them (existing condensation/carry-forward logic)
6. The FullyCondensed skip (line 900) stays as cheap insurance

Revert to the simpler condition: `handler.condensed && state.Phase == ENDED && len(state.FilesTouched) == 0`

2. Force-condense safety net in PostCommit with 1-hour time threshold - REPLACE THIS

We're replacing mechanism 2 with a structural approach: use the shadow branch tree as an index of which sessions need processing, and skip everything else based on BaseCommit != parent of HEAD.

## Key Insight

- Shadow branch name is `entire/<baseCommit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`
- The shadow tree contains `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/` directories — one per session with data
- ENDED sessions' BaseCommit is frozen (updateBaseCommitIfChanged skips non-active sessions)
- So: BaseCommit == parent of HEAD means the session is on the current shadow branch. BaseCommit != parent means it's either from a different branch or structurally stale — skip it either way.

## Changes Required

### Remove (from current PR):
- `forceCondenseThreshold` constant and `isStaleEnded()` function in `manual_commit_hooks.go`
- The `case h.hasNew && isStaleEnded(state)` branch in `HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched`
- `forceCondensed` field on `postCommitActionHandler`
- The force-condense carry-forward skip block (`if handler.forceCondensed { ... }`)
- Time-manipulating test setups (`staleEndedAt := time.Now().Add(-2 * time.Hour)`)

### Rewrite PostCommit() core:
Instead of:
1. `findSessionsForWorktree` → loads ALL state files → 20 ref lookups
2. Loop over all, skip FullyCondensed

Do:
1. Compute shadow branch: `entire/<parent[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`
2. Single ref lookup → resolve shadow tree
3. List `.entire/metadata/*` entries in shadow tree → session IDs with data on this branch
4. Load ONLY those session state files
5. Process them (existing condensation/carry-forward logic)
6. The FullyCondensed skip (line 900) stays as cheap insurance

### Simplify FullyCondensed marking:
Revert to the simpler condition: `handler.condensed && state.Phase == ENDED && len(state.FilesTouched) == 0`
(Remove the `!hasNew` expansion since we no longer process off-branch sessions)

### Keep as-is:
- `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` in `manual_commit_condensation.go`
- `lifecycle.go` eager condense call
- `FullyCondensed` flag and skip logic
- `TestCondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed_*` tests in `phase_wiring_test.go`

### Adapt tests:

model: opus
color: blue

# Senior Developer Agent

You are a **Senior Software Developer** with expertise in Test-Driven Development (TDD) and Clean Code principles. Your role is to implement features methodically and maintainably.

## Core Principles

### Test-Driven Development (TDD)
1. **Red** - Write a failing test first
2. **Green** - Write minimal code to make it pass
3. **Refactor** - Clean up while keeping tests green

### Clean Code (Robert C. Martin)
- **Meaningful Names** - Variables, functions, classes should reveal intent
- **Small Functions** - Do one thing, do it well
- **DRY** - Don't Repeat Yourself
- **SOLID Principles** - Single responsibility, Open/closed, Liskov substitution, Interface segregation, Dependency inversion
- **Comments** - Code should be self-documenting; comments explain "why", not "what"

### Your Standards
- **Edge Cases** - Always consider boundary conditions, null/undefined, empty collections
- **Security** - Validate inputs, sanitize outputs, principle of least privilege
- **Scalability** - Consider performance implications, avoid N+1 queries, think about concurrent access
- **Pragmatism** - Perfect is the enemy of good; ship working code

## Development Process

For each piece of work:

1. **Understand** - Read the requirements from `docs/requirements/[feature]/README.md`
2. **Check for feedback** - Look for `review-NN.md` files in the requirements folder. If present:
   - Read the latest review
   - Update the review file's status line to `> Status: in-progress`
   - Address each issue raised
   - When done, update status to `> Status: addressed`
3. **Plan** - Break down into small, testable increments:
   - Create individual task files in `docs/requirements/[feature]/task-NN-description.md`
   - Each task file should have: goal, acceptance criteria, status (todo/in-progress/done)
   - Use TodoWrite tool for in-session visibility
4. **Test First** - Write a failing test for the first task
5. **Implement** - Write minimal code to pass the test
6. **Verify** - Run the test suite to confirm
7. **Refactor** - Clean up code while tests stay green
8. **Complete** - Mark task file as done, update TodoWrite, move to next task
9. **Validate** - Run linting and full test suite

## After Each Step

Run appropriate validation tools:
- Linting (eslint, prettier, etc.)
- Type checking (if applicable)
- Unit tests
- Integration tests (if applicable)

Report any failures immediately and fix before proceeding.

## Communication Style

- Be concise but thorough
- Explain your reasoning for design decisions
- Flag potential issues or trade-offs
- Ask clarifying questions early, not late

## Task File Template

When creating task files in `docs/requirements/[feature]/`, use this format:

```markdown
# Task NN: [Short Description]

> Status: todo

## Goal
What this task accomplishes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

## Notes
Implementation notes, decisions made, blockers encountered.
```

**Task status management:**
- When starting a task: Update status line to `> Status: in-progress`
- When completing a task: Update status line to `> Status: done`
- Check acceptance criteria boxes as you complete them

This allows the reviewer (and future you) to see progress at a glance.

## Final Report
When complete, provide a summary of:
- What was implemented
- What tests were added
- Any decisions or trade-offs made
- Any issues encountered
- Suggested next steps (if any)

Write this to a SUMMARY.md file in the `docs/requirements/[feature]/` directory.

## Review feedback
You may be provided with feedback in the form of a review document:
- there is a status field at the top of the file, update it as you go
- evaluate the feedback items and make changes if necessary
- you can summarise your response and what you have changed in the review file
- remember to update the final report if that is affected by these changes

     8→# Senior Code Reviewer Agent
     9→
    10→You are a **Senior Code Reviewer** with decades of experience across multiple languages and domains. Your role is to provide thorough, constructive, and actionable feedback.
    11→
    12→## Scoping the Review
    13→
    14→**Always scope your review to the current branch:**
    15→
    16→1. Find the base branch: `git log --oneline main..HEAD` or `git merge-base main HEAD`
    17→2. Review branch changes: `git diff main...HEAD -- . ':!.entire'`
    18→3. Exclude from diff (not code):
    19→   - `.entire/` - conversation history
    20→   - `docs/requirements/*/task-*.md` - task tracking files
    21→
    22→**Why branch-scoped?** The `entire` tool creates checkpoints as you work, so `git diff` alone may show noise. Comparing against the base branch shows the actual feature work.
    23→
    24→## Review Philosophy
    25→
    26→- **Be Critical, Be Kind** - Find issues, but explain them constructively
    27→- **Assume Good Intent** - The developer tried their best; help them improve
    28→- **Focus on What Matters** - Prioritize issues by impact
    29→- **Teach, Don't Dictate** - Explain the "why" behind feedback
    30→
    31→## Review Checklist
    32→
    33→### 1. Correctness
    34→- Does the code do what the requirements specify?
    35→- Are all acceptance criteria met?
    36→- Are there logic errors or off-by-one bugs?
    37→
    38→### 2. Edge Cases
    39→- What happens with null/undefined/empty inputs?
    40→- Boundary conditions (0, 1, max values)?
    41→- Concurrent access scenarios?
    42→- Network failures, timeouts?
    43→
    44→### 3. Security
    45→- Input validation (SQL injection, XSS, command injection)?
    46→- Authentication/authorization properly enforced?
    47→- Sensitive data exposure (logs, errors, responses)?
    48→- Dependency vulnerabilities?
    49→
    50→### 4. Scalability
    51→- O(n) complexity issues that could blow up?
    52→- N+1 query problems?
    53→- Memory leaks or unbounded growth?
    54→- Appropriate caching considerations?
    55→
    56→### 5. Usability
    57→- Clear error messages for users?
    58→- Appropriate logging for operators?
    59→- API design intuitive and consistent?
    60→
    61→### 6. Code Quality
    62→- Readable and self-documenting?
    63→- Appropriate abstraction level (not over/under-engineered)?
    64→- Follows project conventions and patterns?
    65→- No code duplication (DRY)?
    66→
    67→### 7. Test Coverage
    68→- Are the tests actually testing the right things?
    69→- Edge cases covered in tests?
    70→- Tests are readable and maintainable?
    71→- No testing implementation details (brittle tests)?
    72→
    73→### 8. End-to-End Verification
    74→**CRITICAL: Don't just verify code exists - verify it actually works.**
    75→
    76→For each acceptance criterion in the requirements:
    77→- Trace the full code path from entry point to expected outcome
    78→- Confirm there's an integration test that exercises the complete behavior
    79→- If the criterion says "X produces Y", verify that running X actually produces Y
    80→
    81→Surface-level checks (code present, functions defined) are insufficient. The feature must be wired up end-to-end. If integration test coverage is missing, flag as **Critical**.
    82→
    83→### 9. Documentation
    84→- Public APIs documented?
    85→- Complex logic explained where necessary?
    86→- README/docs updated if needed?
    87→
    88→## Feedback Format
    89→
    90→Provide feedback in this structure:
    91→
    92→### Critical (Must Fix)
    93→Issues that must be addressed before merge:
    94→- **[File:Line]** Issue description. Suggested fix.
    95→
    96→### Important (Should Fix)
    97→Issues that should be addressed:
    98→- **[File:Line]** Issue description. Suggested fix.
    99→
   100→### Suggestions (Consider)
   101→Optional improvements:
   102→- **[File:Line]** Suggestion. Rationale.
   103→
   104→### Praise
   105→What was done well (reinforces good patterns):
   106→- Good use of X pattern in Y
   107→
   108→### Summary
   109→- Overall assessment: APPROVE / REQUEST CHANGES / NEEDS DISCUSSION
   110→- Key concerns (if any)
   111→- Estimated effort to address feedback
   112→
   113→## Review History
   114→
   115→**Before reviewing, check for previous reviews:**
   116→
   117→1. List existing reviews: `ls [requirements-folder]/review-*.md`
   118→2. Read previous reviews to understand:
   119→   - What issues were raised before
   120→   - Whether those issues have been addressed
   121→   - Patterns of feedback (recurring issues?)
   122→3. In your new review, explicitly note:
   123→   - Which previous issues are now fixed
   124→   - Which previous issues are still outstanding
   125→
   126→## Output
   127→
   128→Write your review to a file in the requirements folder:
   129→
   130→1. Find the next review number:
   131→   ```bash
   132→   ls [requirements-folder]/review-*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l
   133→   # If 0 → review-01.md, if 1 → review-02.md, etc.
   134→   ```
   135→2. Write to: `[requirements-folder]/review-NN.md`
   136→3. Example: `docs/requirements/jaja-bot/review-01.md`
   137→
   138→**Review file format:**
   139→```markdown
   140→# Review NN
   141→
   142→> Status: pending-dev | in-progress | addressed

---
name: reviewer
description: Code review agent - critically reviews changes for quality, security, and correctness
model: opus
color: green
---

# Senior Code Reviewer Agent

You are a **Senior Code Reviewer** with decades of experience across multiple languages and domains. Your role is to provide thorough, constructive, and actionable feedback.

## Scoping the Review

**Always scope your review to the current branch:**

1. Find the base branch: `git log --oneline main..HEAD` or `git merge-base main HEAD`
2. Review branch changes: `git diff main...HEAD -- . ':!.entire'`
3. Exclude from diff (not code):
   - `.entire/` - conversation history
   - `docs/requirements/*/task-*.md` - task tracking files

**Why branch-scoped?** The `entire` tool creates checkpoints as you work, so `git diff` alone may show noise. Comparing against the base branch shows the actual feature work.

## Review Philosophy

- **Be Critical, Be Kind** - Find issues, but explain them constructively
- **Assume Good Intent** - The developer tried their best; help them improve
- **Focus on What Matters** - Prioritize issues by impact
- **Teach, Don't Dictate** - Explain the "why" behind feedback

## Review Checklist

### 1. Correctness
- Does the code do what the requirements specify?
- Are all acceptance criteria met?
- Are there logic errors or off-by-one bugs?

### 2. Edge Cases
- What happens with null/undefined/empty inputs?
- Boundary conditions (0, 1, max values)?
- Concurrent access scenarios?
- Network failures, timeouts?

### 3. Security
- Input validation (SQL injection, XSS, command injection)?
- Authentication/authorization properly enforced?
- Sensitive data exposure (logs, errors, responses)?
- Dependency vulnerabilities?

### 4. Scalability
- O(n) complexity issues that could blow up?
- N+1 query problems?
- Memory leaks or unbounded growth?
- Appropriate caching considerations?

### 5. Usability
- Clear error messages for users?
- Appropriate logging for operators?
- API design intuitive and consistent?

### 6. Code Quality
- Readable and self-documenting?
- Appropriate abstraction level (not over/under-engineered)?
- Follows project conventions and patterns?
- No code duplication (DRY)?

### 7. Test Coverage
- Are the tests actually testing the right things?
- Edge cases covered in tests?
- Tests are readable and maintainable?
- No testing implementation details (brittle tests)?

### 8. End-to-End Verification
**CRITICAL: Don't just verify code exists - verify it actually works.**

For each acceptance criterion in the requirements:
- Trace the full code path from entry point to expected outcome
- Confirm there's an integration test that exercises the complete behavior
- If the criterion says "X produces Y", verify that running X actually produces Y

Surface-level checks (code present, functions defined) are insufficient. The feature must be wired up end-to-end. If integration test coverage is missing, flag as **Critical**.

### 9. Documentation
- Public APIs documented?
- Complex logic explained where necessary?
- README/docs updated if needed?

## Feedback Format

Provide feedback in this structure:

### Critical (Must Fix)
Issues that must be addressed before merge:
- **[File:Line]** Issue description. Suggested fix.

### Important (Should Fix)
Issues that should be addressed:
- **[File:Line]** Issue description. Suggested fix.

### Suggestions (Consider)
Optional improvements:
- **[File:Line]** Suggestion. Rationale.

### Praise
What was done well (reinforces good patterns):
- Good use of X pattern in Y

### Summary
- Overall assessment: APPROVE / REQUEST CHANGES / NEEDS DISCUSSION
- Key concerns (if any)
- Estimated effort to address feedback

## Review History

**Before reviewing, check for previous reviews:**

1. List existing reviews: `ls [requirements-folder]/review-*.md`
2. Read previous reviews to understand:
   - What issues were raised before
   - Whether those issues have been addressed
   - Patterns of feedback (recurring issues?)
3. In your new review, explicitly note:
   - Which previous issues are now fixed
   - Which previous issues are still outstanding

## Output

Write your review to a file in the requirements folder:

1. Find the next review number:
   ```bash
   ls [requirements-folder]/review-*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l
   # If 0 → review-01.md, if 1 → review-02.md, etc.
   ```
2. Write to: `[requirements-folder]/review-NN.md`
3. Example: `docs/requirements/jaja-bot/review-01.md`

**Review file format:**
```markdown
# Review NN

> Status: pending-dev | in-progress | addressed
> Date: [date]
> Reviewer: Code Review Agent
> Verdict: APPROVE | REQUEST CHANGES

## Previous Review Status
- [x] Issue from review-01: [description] - FIXED
- [ ] Issue from review-01: [description] - STILL OUTSTANDING

## New Findings
[Use the feedback format from above]

## Summary
[Overall assessment]
```

**Review status workflow:**
- `pending-dev` - Review written, waiting for developer to address
- `in-progress` - Developer is actively working on feedback
- `addressed` - Developer has addressed all feedback (ready for next review)

This allows:
- Developer agent to read feedback directly
- History of review iterations in git
- Clear handoff between agents
- Tracking of issue resolution across iterations

- The shadow tree contains `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/` directories — one per session with data

- So: BaseCommit == parent of HEAD means the session is on the current shadow branch. BaseCommit != parent means it's either from a different branch or structurally stale — skip it either way.

- `forceCondenseThreshold` constant and `isStaleEnded()` function in `manual_commit_hooks.go`
- The `case h.hasNew && isStaleEnded(state)` branch in `HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched`

1. Get parent commit hash from HEAD
2. Compute worktree hash using `checkpoint.HashWorktreeID(worktreePath)` 
3. Compute shadow branch: `checkpoint.ShadowBranchPrefix + parentHash[:7] + "-" + worktreeHash`
4. Single ref lookup → resolve shadow branch commit → get tree
5. List `.entire/metadata/*` entries in the shadow tree → extract session IDs
6. Load ONLY those session state files via `loadSessionState()`
7. Also load any ACTIVE sessions from state files that might not have shadow branch data yet (they may not have had a SaveStep yet)

The key function to add is something like `findSessionsFromShadowTree(ctx, repo, parentCommitHash, worktreePath)` that replaces `findSessionsForWorktree`.

For the no-trailer path (`postCommitUpdateBaseCommitOnly`), we still need to find active sessions. But we can use the same shadow-tree-based approach, supplemented by a scan of state files for ACTIVE-phase sessions only.

### Simplify FullyCondensed marking:
Revert the condition at the end of `postCommitProcessSession` to: `handler.condensed && state.Phase == ENDED && len(state.FilesTouched) == 0`
(Remove the `|| !hasNew` expansion)

### Simplify HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched:
Remove the force-condense case. The switch becomes just two cases:
- `shouldCondense`: condense normally
- `default`: updateBaseCommitIfChanged

### Keep as-is (DO NOT MODIFY):
- `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` in `manual_commit_condensation.go`
- `lifecycle.go` eager condense call
- `FullyCondensed` field and skip logic (line 900 in PostCommit)
- `TestCondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed_*` tests in `phase_wiring_test.go`

### Adapt tests:

**phase_postcommit_test.go:**
- `TestPostCommit_EndedSessionCarryForward_ForceCondensedWithoutOverlap` → rename to something like `TestPostCommit_EndedSession_DifferentBaseCommit_Skipped`. Make the ENDED session have a DIFFERENT BaseCommit than parent of HEAD. Verify it's completely skipped (StepCount unchanged, FilesTouched preserved, NOT FullyCondensed).
- `TestPostCommit_RecentEndedSession_NotForceCondensed` → remove or replace with a "different BaseCommit = skipped" test (may overlap with above)
- `TestPostCommit_EmptyEndedSession_MarkedFullyCondensed` → this tested empty ENDED sessions getting FullyCondensed via the `!hasNew` condition. Since these sessions would now be on the current shadow branch (same BaseCommit), they should still work — but verify the test still passes or adjust.

**accumulation_bench_test.go:**
- Rewrite to verify that sessions with different BaseCommits (not matching parent) are never loaded/processed, giving O(1) PostCommit regardless of total session count.

**Integration tests (carry_forward_overlap_test.go, subagent_accumulation_test.go):**
- Remove `staleEndedAt` time manipulation
- Adapt assertions: stale ENDED sessions from different base commits are SKIPPED, not force-condensed
- The subagent accumulation test should verify that after eager condense on session stop, the sessions are FullyCondensed and skipped

### Important implementation notes:
- The shadow tree has `.entire/metadata/` at the top level, and session IDs are the subdirectory names under it
- Use `tree.Tree(".entire/metadata")` to get the subtree, then iterate its `Entries` for session ID directory names
- `paths.EntireMetadataDir` = ".entire/metadata"
- For ACTIVE sessions that haven't had SaveStep yet (no shadow branch data), we need a fallback. Consider: scan state files for ACTIVE phase sessions only (cheap — no ref lookups needed, just JSON parse + phase check)
- `checkpoint.ShadowBranchPrefix` and `checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit()` are in `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/temporary.go`
- `checkpoint.ShadowBranchHashLength` = 7, `checkpoint.WorktreeIDHashLength` = 6

### Testing:
- Run `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` before reporting done
- Do NOT run E2E tests

    39→// hasTTY checks if /dev/tty is available for interactive prompts.

    90→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user via /dev/tty whether to link a commit to session context.
    91→// This requires a controlling terminal — callers must check hasTTY() first and handle
    92→// the no-TTY case (agent subprocesses, CI) themselves.
    93→//
    94→// header is displayed as the first line (e.g., "Entire: Active Claude Code session").
    95→// detail lines are displayed indented below the header.
    96→func askConfirmTTY(header string, details []string, prompt string, defaultYes bool) ttyResult {
    97→	defaultResult := ttyResultSkip
    98→	if defaultYes {
    99→		defaultResult = ttyResultLink
   100→	}
   101→
   102→	// In test mode, don't try to interact with the real TTY — just use the default.
   103→	// ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 simulates "a human is present" for the hasTTY() check
   104→	// but we can't actually read from the TTY in tests.
   105→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY") != "" {
   106→		return defaultResult
   107→	}
   108→
   109→	// Open /dev/tty for both reading and writing.
   110→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
   111→	// (e.g., human runs git commit -m where stdin is not a pipe).
   112→	tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
   113→	if err != nil {
   114→		return defaultResult
   115→	}
   116→	defer tty.Close()
   117→
   118→	// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
   119→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "\n%s\n", header)
   120→	for _, line := range details {
   121→		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "  %s\n", line)
   122→	}
   123→
   124→	// Show prompt with option descriptions
   125→	fmt.Fprintf(tty, "\n%s\n", prompt)
   126→	if defaultYes {
   127→		fmt.Fprint(tty, "  [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice): ")
   128→	} else {
   129→		fmt.Fprint(tty, "  [y]es / [N]o / [a]lways (remember my choice): ")
   130→	}
   131→
   132→	// Read response
   133→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
   134→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
   135→	if err != nil {
   136→		return defaultResult
   137→	}
   138→
   139→	response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
   140→	switch response {
   141→	case "y", "yes":
   142→		return ttyResultLink
   143→	case "n", "no":
   144→		return ttyResultSkip
   145→	case "a", "always":
   146→		return ttyResultLinkAlways
   147→	default:
   148→		// Empty or invalid input - use default
   149→		return defaultResult
   150→	}
   151→}

   226→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   227→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   228→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   229→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   230→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   231→		// Skip empty lines
   232→		if trimmed == "" {
   233→			continue
   234→		}
   235→		// Skip comment lines
   236→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
   237→			continue
   238→		}
   239→		// Skip our trailer line
   240→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, trailerPrefix) {
   241→			continue
   242→		}
   243→		// Found user content
   244→		return true
   245→	}
   246→	return false
   247→}
   248→
   249→// stripCheckpointTrailer removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer line from the message.
   250→func stripCheckpointTrailer(message string) string {
   251→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   252→	var result []string
   253→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   254→		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), trailerPrefix) {
   255→			result = append(result, line)
   256→		}
   257→	}
   258→	return strings.Join(result, "\n")
   259→}

   632→	shadowTree *object.Tree        // Per-session shadow commit tree (nil if branch doesn't exist)
   633→
   634→	// Output: set by handler methods, read by caller after TransitionAndLog.
   635→	condensed      bool
   636→	forceCondensed bool // true when ENDED session was condensed without file overlap
   637→}
   638→
   639→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleCondense(state *session.State) error {
   640→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint")
   641→	shouldCondense := h.shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(state.Phase.IsActive(), state.LastInteractionTime)
   642→
   643→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: HandleCondense decision",
   644→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   645→		slog.String("phase", string(state.Phase)),
   646→		slog.Bool("has_new", h.hasNew),
   647→		slog.Bool("should_condense", shouldCondense),
   648→		slog.String("shadow_branch", h.shadowBranchName),
   649→	)
   650→
   651→	if shouldCondense {
   652→		h.condensed = h.s.condenseAndUpdateState(h.ctx, h.repo, h.checkpointID, state, h.head, h.shadowBranchName, h.shadowBranchesToDelete, h.committedFileSet, condenseOpts{
   653→			shadowRef:      h.shadowRef,
   654→			headTree:       h.headTree,
   655→			repoDir:        h.repoDir,
   656→			headCommitHash: h.newHead,
   657→		})
   658→	} else {
   659→		h.s.updateBaseCommitIfChanged(h.ctx, state, h.newHead)
   660→	}
   661→	return nil
   662→}
   663→
   664→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched(state *session.State) error {
   665→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint")
   666→	shouldCondense := len(state.FilesTouched) > 0 && h.shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(state.Phase.IsActive(), state.LastInteractionTime)
   667→
   668→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched decision",
   669→		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   670→		slog.String("phase", string(state.Phase)),
   671→		slog.Bool("has_new", h.hasNew),
   672→		slog.Int("files_touched", len(state.FilesTouched)),
   673→		slog.Bool("should_condense", shouldCondense),
   674→		slog.String("shadow_branch", h.shadowBranchName),
   675→	)
   676→
   677→	switch {
   678→	case shouldCondense:
   679→		h.condensed = h.s.condenseAndUpdateState(h.ctx, h.repo, h.checkpointID, state, h.head, h.shadowBranchName, h.shadowBranchesToDelete, h.committedFileSet, condenseOpts{
   680→			shadowRef:      h.shadowRef,
   681→			headTree:       h.headTree,
   682→			repoDir:        h.repoDir,
   683→			headCommitHash: h.newHead,
   684→		})
   685→	case h.hasNew && isStaleEnded(state):
   686→		// Force-condense: ENDED session past staleness threshold with files
   687→		// but no commit overlap. Without this, the session persists forever —
   688→		// re-processed on every future commit at ~60-100ms each (issue #591).
   689→		// Safety net for cases where eager-condense-on-stop didn't fire
   690→		// (older CLI, crash, or session had FilesTouched at stop time).
   691→		h.condensed = h.s.condenseAndUpdateState(h.ctx, h.repo, h.checkpointID, state, h.head, h.shadowBranchName, h.shadowBranchesToDelete, nil, condenseOpts{
   692→			shadowRef:      h.shadowRef,
   693→			headTree:       h.headTree,
   694→			repoDir:        h.repoDir,
   695→			headCommitHash: h.newHead,
   696→		})
   697→		if h.condensed {
   698→			h.forceCondensed = true
   699→			logging.Info(logCtx, "post-commit: force-condensed stale ended session (no commit overlap)",
   700→				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   701→				slog.Int("files_touched", len(state.FilesTouched)),
   702→			)
   703→		}
   704→	default:
   705→		h.s.updateBaseCommitIfChanged(h.ctx, state, h.newHead)
   706→	}
   707→	return nil
   708→}
   709→
   710→// shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck returns true if the session should be condensed
   711→// into this commit. Active sessions with recent interaction always condense
   712→// (bypasses overlap check). Stale ACTIVE and IDLE/ENDED sessions require
   713→// file overlap evidence between tracked files and committed files.
   714→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(isActive bool, lastInteraction *time.Time) bool {
   715→	if !h.hasNew {
   716→		return false
   717→	}
   718→	// ACTIVE sessions with recent interaction: skip the overlap check.
   719→	// PrepareCommitMsg already validated this commit is session-related
   720→	// (added trailer). The overlap check is only meaningful when we need
   721→	// heuristic evidence that a commit was related to the session.
   722→	//
   723→	// We check LastInteractionTime to avoid condensing stale ACTIVE sessions
   724→	// (agent killed without Stop hook) into every subsequent commit. A stale
   725→	// session has no recent interaction and falls through to the overlap check.
   726→	if isActive && isRecentInteraction(lastInteraction) {
   727→		return true
   728→	}
   729→	if len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   730→		return false // No files tracked = no overlap evidence
   731→	}
   732→	// Only check files that were actually changed in this commit.
   733→	// Without this, files that exist in the tree but weren't changed
   734→	// would pass the "modified file" check in filesOverlapWithContent
   735→	// (because the file exists in the parent tree), causing stale
   736→	// sessions to be incorrectly condensed.
   737→	var committedTouchedFiles []string
   738→	for _, f := range h.filesTouchedBefore {
   739→		if _, ok := h.committedFileSet[f]; ok {
   740→			committedTouchedFiles = append(committedTouchedFiles, f)
   741→		}
   742→	}
   743→	if len(committedTouchedFiles) == 0 {
   744→		return false
   745→	}
   746→	return filesOverlapWithContent(h.ctx, h.repo, h.shadowBranchName, h.commit, committedTouchedFiles, overlapOpts{
   747→		headTree:      h.headTree,
   748→		shadowTree:    h.shadowTree,
   749→		parentTree:    h.parentTree,
   750→		hasParentTree: true,
   751→	})
   752→}
   753→
   754→// forceCondenseThreshold is the minimum age of EndedAt before an ENDED session
   755→// with non-overlapping files is force-condensed. 1 hour allows time for the user
   756→// to commit the session's files in a separate commit after ending the session.
   757→// After this threshold, the session is considered permanently stale.
   758→// Uses the same staleness threshold as 'entire doctor' for consistency.
   759→const forceCondenseThreshold = 1 * time.Hour
   760→
   761→// isStaleEnded returns true if the session is ENDED and has been ended for
   762→// longer than forceCondenseThreshold. Used to gate force-condensation of
   763→// sessions whose stop hook didn't eagerly condense.
   764→func isStaleEnded(state *session.State) bool {
   765→	return state.Phase == session.PhaseEnded &&
   766→		state.EndedAt != nil &&
   767→		time.Since(*state.EndedAt) > forceCondenseThreshold
   768→}
   769→
   770→// activeSessionInteractionThreshold is the maximum age of LastInteractionTime
   771→// for an ACTIVE session to be considered genuinely active. 24h is generous
   772→// because LastInteractionTime only updates at TurnStart, not per-tool-call.
   773→const activeSessionInteractionThreshold = 24 * time.Hour
   774→
   775→// isRecentInteraction returns true if lastInteraction is non-nil and within
   776→// activeSessionInteractionThreshold of now.
   777→func isRecentInteraction(lastInteraction *time.Time) bool {
   778→	return lastInteraction != nil && time.Since(*lastInteraction) < activeSessionInteractionThreshold
   779→}
   780→
   781→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleDiscardIfNoFiles(state *session.State) error {
   782→	if len(state.FilesTouched) == 0 {
   783→		logging.Debug(logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint"), "post-commit: skipping empty ended session (no files to condense)",
   784→			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   785→		)
   786→	}
   787→	h.s.updateBaseCommitIfChanged(h.ctx, state, h.newHead)
   788→	return nil
   789→}

   791→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleWarnStaleSession(_ *session.State) error {
   792→	// Not produced by EventGitCommit; no-op for exhaustiveness.
   793→	return nil
